questions.question: How is “optimization” best defined for a single‑purpose processor according to the provided material?

options.A: Making the processor programmable after fabrication
options.B: Tailoring the fixed hardware so that it executes one dedicated task very quickly and with low power use
options.C: Adding a large instruction set to support many applications
options.D: Integrating external memory to expand capability

questions.explanation:
Optimization for a single‑purpose processor means the hardware is fixed and tuned for a specific operation, yielding very fast and power‑efficient performance (see Page 44).  

---

questions.question: Which parameters are explicitly mentioned as being considered when optimizing a single‑purpose processor?

options.B: Execution speed for the dedicated task, power consumption, and dedicated functionality
options.C: Number of cores, cache size, and operating‑system support
options.D: Wireless connectivity, display resolution, and battery life

questions.explanation:
The context states that a single‑purpose processor is “very fast and power‑efficient for that single function,” indicating speed and power as key optimization parameters (see Page 44).  

---

questions.question: Compared with a general‑purpose processor, the performance of a single‑purpose processor is described as:

options.B: Very fast and power‑efficient for its single function
options.C: Moderately fast with average power use
options.D: Always lower in power consumption but also lower in speed

questions.explanation:
Page 44 notes the high speed and power efficiency of a single‑purpose processor, whereas Page 41 describes general‑purpose processors as having “moderate” performance.  

---

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the design approach of a single‑purpose processor?

options.A: It uses programmable microcode to support many tasks.
options.B: Its hardware is fixed and optimized for a specific operation.
options.C: It relies on external memory for instruction storage.
options.D: It employs a complex instruction set for versatility.

questions.explanation:
The design description for a single‑purpose processor emphasizes “hardware is fixed and optimized for that specific operation” (Page 44).  

---

questions.question: The motor‑controller unit cited as an example of a single‑purpose processor is efficient mainly because:

options.A: It can run multiple applications after fabrication.
options.B: Its hardware is fixed and tailored specifically to motor‑control tasks.
options.C: It includes a large on‑chip cache.
options.D: Its clock frequency can vary widely during operation.

questions.explanation:
The example (motor‑controller unit) is listed under single‑purpose processors, whose efficiency derives from dedicated, fixed hardware (Page 44).  

---

questions.question: Why does the text describe a general‑purpose processor as a “programmable single‑purpose processor”?

options.A: Because it has a fixed instruction set.
options.B: Because it executes a stored sequence of instructions, similar to a single‑purpose processor that runs a dedicated program.
options.C: Because it cannot be reprogrammed after fabrication.

questions.explanation:
Page 105 explains that a GPP “executes a sequence of instructions stored in program memory,” making it essentially a programmable single‑purpose processor.  

---

questions.question: To improve power‑efficiency of a single‑purpose processor, which design change aligns with the optimization concept described?

options.B: Removing or simplifying logic that is not required for the dedicated task.

questions.explanation:
Since optimization relies on fixed, task‑specific hardware (Page 44), eliminating unnecessary logic directly enhances power efficiency.  

---

questions.question: Which of the following examples from the context best illustrates a single‑purpose processor optimized for a specific function?
questions.explanation:
The JPEC codec is explicitly listed as an example of a single‑purpose processor (Page 44).  

---

questions.question: The statement “Not programmable after fabrication” for single‑purpose processors implies which effect on the optimization process?

options.A: Post‑fabrication software updates can improve performance.
options.B: All optimization must be completed during hardware design, before fabrication.
options.C: The processor can readily run multiple operating systems.
options.D: Larger external memory is required to compensate for lack of flexibility.

questions.explanation:
Page 44 notes the lack of post‑fabrication programmability, meaning optimization decisions are fixed at design time.  

---

questions.question: Which metric would be the least appropriate for evaluating the optimization of a single‑purpose processor, based on the context?

options.A: Execution speed for its dedicated task
options.C: Ability to run arbitrary software applications
options.D: Hardware area devoted to the specific function

questions.explanation: Single‑purpose processors are described as “Not programmable after fabrication” (Page 44), so their ability to run arbitrary applications is not a relevant optimization metric.
